submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on content-bearing tokens of expository/reference prose: numerals, dates, ordinals and quantities (' six', ' twenty', ' 2009', ' 27', ' third', 'hundreds', 'percent'), place and person names (' France', ' Canada', ' India', 'Sanchez', ' Livingston'), spatial and measurement words (' north', ' toward', 'direction', ' side', 'thickness', 'density'), technical or scientific nouns ('devices', 'technologies', 'methods', 'types', 'particles', 'experiment') and the reporting or study verbs that present findings ('showed', 'announced', 'reported', 'demonstrate', 'indicate', 'revealed'); it also peaks on the word-final subword piece of a multi-token name or on a LaTeX or math symbol ('nu', ' dx', 'quad', '\{'), and in the scan roughly 40-47% of tokens in these classes clear the activity line against 16% of all tokens. It stays below the line on articles, pronouns and conjunctions ('the', 'a', 'of', 'and', 'he', 'she', 'we', 'it' - only 3% of determiner tokens are active) and on everyday concrete or narrative nouns ('food', 'fear', 'life', 'woman', 'war', 'room').

Ghana is a Republic located in Western Africa and is a member of the West African Union.
Ghana's economic decline only worsened after doomsday, and aid came in the form of the new democratic government of Nigeria, as well as the Ivory Coast. In exchange for aid, Jerry Rawlings current leader of Ghana was required to begin democratizing. Elections overseen by Ivory Coast and Nigeria saw Rawlings elected democratically by a narrow margin in 1993. The relationship forged continued and in 1999 along with Senegal and Togo, the nations formed the West African Union.
Ghana is a parliamentary democracy divided amongst a president, parliament, cabinet, council of state, and an independent judiciary. The government transitioned in 1993 from a military dictatorship under Rawlings to a civilian lead government.
The nation of Nigeria aided Ghana's transition to a democratic state. It sent officials to oversee the elections and ensured a fair and equal vote.
The President is both the head of state and the head of government. He or she must be a natural born Ghanian citizen, at least 40 years of age, and be a qualified citizen eligible for Congress.
The president is responsible for upholding the Constitution, act on executive authority of the Republic of Ghana, and keep the national security and territorial integrity of the nation.
The president is also given the power to lead the executive branch of government; act as the commander in chief of the armed forces and declare war; issue executive orders, medals, and pardons; as well as declare martial law and a state of emergency.
The Ghanaian Parliament is a unicameral system with the Parliament as the legislative body. There are 275 seats in the Parliament, and are divided up by party. Each of the ten states are divided up into Parliament constituencies. They range from 11 seats to 47 seats per state.
Members of Parliament, or MP's are elected by popular vote. The elections are operate on the first- past the post. There are two majority parties and several minority parties.

ASP.NET Core encourages the use of dependency injection by the built-in DI container. This feature of ASP.NET Core is very handy as many extensions such as logging and configuration via IOptions pattern are registered using during startup in Startup.cs. ASP.NET Core registers these services, along with any custom services you need using the built-in DI container via IServiceCollection.
This feature of ASP.NET Core can be utilized for dependency injection in Azure Functions V2 as it comes with .NET Core. We can create a container by creating an instance of IServiceCollection and then registering the services we need.
Function app project. Azure.Functions.v2.DI.FunctionApp. This is the project that contains an HTTP-triggered Azure function, which returns the list of time zones via an HTTP GET.
Helper project. Azure.Functions.v2.DI.Helpers. As the name suggests this contains helper class to read from Azure blob storage. The blob file containing a JSON array of time zones is stored in a file named timezones.json in a container azfnv2demo.
Services project. Azure.Functions.v2.DI.Services. This project contains the TimeZoneService class that returns data to the function project by reading data from the Azure blob via the helper project.
This means that the Function app project has a dependency on the services project, and services project has a dependency on the helper project.
As you would have noticed in the code above, a new object of AzureBlobStorageHelper is created which is then used to get the data from blob storage. However, this makes my TimeZoneService.cs code difficult to unit test. What we need is to inject an instance of IAzureBlobStorageHelper, when an instance of TimeZoneService is created.
The first thing we do is make a change in TimeZoneService.cs in Services project to remove the instantiation of AzureBlobStorageHelper and have it injected in the constructor. The constructor of TimeZoneService can also include other dependencies such as ILogger for logging, HttpClient for REST calls etc, but those are left out for the sake of this example.
The next step is to register the services and build the ServiceProvider. This is done by creating an instance of IServiceCollection, registering the services and then making a call to the BuildServiceProvider method on the ServiceCollection. This returns the ServiceProvider that has all the registrations and other configuration if we used it, such as adding logging. adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The house stood at the end of the lane, and the mother kept the fire going while the boy and the girl played on the floor. There was bread on the table and soup in the pot, and the smell of it filled the kitchen. Outside, the wind pushed at the door, and the dog slept near the warmth with his head on his paws. The father came in late with mud on his boots and hung his coat behind the door. Nobody spoke for a while. The girl asked about the noise in the barn, and the mother said it was only the boards moving in the wind. The boy watched the flames and thought about the field behind the house, where the grass was long and the birds hid in it. The father took a bowl and sat down, and the fear that had been in the room all day went out of him. They ate together and listened to the fire.

Later, the mother washed the bowls in the sink and the girl dried them with a cloth. The dog moved to the door and whined, so the boy let him out into the dark. Above the field the sky was clear, and the cold air smelled of leaves and smoke. The boy stood on the step until the mother called him in. The house was warm and the rooms were quiet, and everyone slept well. In the morning the rain came, and the lane turned to mud, and the roof leaked over the stairs. The father put a bucket under the drip and went out to the barn. The girl fed the hens and the boy carried wood. The mother made bread and the kitchen filled with steam.

They worked and ate and slept, and the days went by. When the spring came, the grass in the field grew high, and the birds came back to the barn. The girl found a nest in the rafters and told the boy, who climbed up to see it. The mother called them for supper, and they ran across the yard with the dog at their heels. The fire was bright that night, and the house was full of talk and laughter. The fear of the winter was gone, and the rooms seemed larger than before. The father said the roof would need work before the cold returned, and the mother nodded and put more wood on the fire. They sat together until the flames sank, and then they went up the stairs to their beds.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Between 2008 and 2013, a team of researchers from the University of Edinburgh surveyed the coastline of northern Norway, measuring the thickness of the ice and the density of the surface layers. The project, led by Dr. Katherine Lindqvist, was announced in a preliminary report and later described in a monograph published in 2014. The methods were simple. Each spring, the team drilled through the ice at fixed stations and recorded the depth of the snow above it. Samples were packed into insulated devices and shipped to the laboratory in Tromsø, where technicians measured the concentration of salts and the size of the particles suspended in the meltwater.

The first results showed a clear pattern. The ice near the shore was thinner than the ice farther north, and the difference increased toward the end of the season. In 2011, the group reported that the average thickness had fallen by 27 centimetres since the beginning of the survey, a figure that was later revised to 31 centimetres after the instruments were recalibrated. Dr. Lindqvist indicated that the trend was consistent with warmer water moving in from the Atlantic, though she cautioned that the record was too short to be conclusive.

A second expedition in 2013 extended the survey to the east, toward the Russian border. The researchers used new technologies, including a sonar device mounted on a sled, and compared the readings with satellite data from the same weeks. The comparison revealed a systematic offset of about 4 percent, which the team attributed to the angle of the beam. Subsequent experiments in a tank confirmed the correction, and the adjusted values were published in the following year.

Several observations remain unexplained. The density of the surface layers varied more than the models predicted, especially in the bays where fresh water drained from the land. The biologists on the team collected samples of algae and small organisms and reported that the communities differed between the thin and thick ice. Whether these differences matter for the larger animals that feed on them is not yet known. A follow-up study, funded in 2016, will measure the same stations with a different method and compare the results. The authors concluded that long records are essential, and that the coast should be monitored for at least another decade. A final report is expected in 2020.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long expository report packed with years, numerals, person and place names, measurement and technical nouns and reporting verbs, testing the active claim deep inside a passage the examples' length cannot explain.
